id: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)
title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
about: Three gunslingers race each other to a fortune in gold buried in a Civil War cemetery.
cue: Serve the mains when Angel Eyes sits down to eat at the farmer's table.
faces: Serve the mains when Angel Eyes sits down to eat at the farmer's table.
“Eat now, talk later. I don't trust a man who chats over his beans.” Tuco
Fried corn chips with chilli salt and a smoky charred tomato and onion salsa
Crispy roast potato coins with garlic aioli

Tuco's spaghetti with beef and pork ragù

Sad Hill Trading PostThe Good, the Bad and the UglyThree gunslingers. One big feed.Every recipe serves 4.

    StartersDesert crossing tortilla chipsFried corn chips with chilli salt and a smoky charred tomato and onion salsaHow to make it12 corn tortillas500ml vegetable oil, for frying1 tsp salt1 tsp chilli powder4 tomatoes1/2 onion1 lime, juicedCut the tortillas into wedges.Fry in the oil at 180°C until crisp, then toss in salt and chilli powder.Char the tomatoes and onion in a dry pan until blackened.Chop together with lime juice and salt for a smoky salsa.Serve with the chips.Gold coin potato roundsCrispy roast potato coins with garlic aioliHow to make it800g small potatoes, sliced in thick coins3 tbsp olive oil1 tsp salt1 clove of garlic, crushed150g mayonnaiseHeat the oven to 220°C. Slice the potatoes and toss in oil and salt.Spread on a tray and roast, turning once.Stir the garlic into mayonnaise for aioli.Pile the coins beside the aioli.MainsFarmhouse bean stewBorlotti beans simmered with smoked ham hock, tomatoes and rosemaryHow to make it400g dried borlotti beans2 tbsp olive oil1 onion, diced3 cloves of garlic1 smoked ham hock1 tin of crushed tomatoes2 sprigs of rosemary1 loaf of Italian breadSoak the beans overnight and drain.Soften the onion and garlic in the oil.Add the beans, ham hock, tomatoes, rosemary and water to cover.Simmer until thick.Shred the ham back in and serve with bread.Tuco's spaghetti with beef and pork ragùTuco's brother at the missionHow to make itAs written, serves 4Spaghetti tossed through a slow-cooked beef and pork ragù with red wine and tomato, finished with pecorino, chilli oil and torn basil.Brown 500g beef mince and 300g pork mince.Add 1 diced onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick and 3 garlic cloves and cook 8 minutes.Pour in 150ml red wine, then 2 tins crushed tomatoes and 2 tbsp tomato paste, and simmer gently for 2 hours, adding water if needed.Cook 500g spaghetti, toss through the ragù with a splash of pasta water, then top with grated pecorino, chilli oil and basil.SweetsSad Hill chocolate mousse cupsDark chocolate mousse in cups with a chocolate coin buried in eachHow to make it200g dark chocolate3 eggs, separated300ml thickened cream4 chocolate coins8 chocolate biscuits, crushedMelt the chocolate and cool slightly.Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks and whip the cream.Fold the yolks into the chocolate, then fold in the cream and whites.Spoon into cups with a chocolate coin buried in each.Chill.Top with crushed biscuits.DrinksBlondie's rye old fashionedRye whisky, demerara syrup and orange bitters stirred over a big ice cubeHow to make it60g demerara sugar60ml hot water240ml rye whisky8 dashes of orange bitters3 cups ice1 orange, peel onlyStir the sugar with the hot water until dissolved, then cool.Stir the whisky, syrup and bitters with ice.Strain over a large ice cube in a heavy glass.Twist orange peel over the top and drop it in.
